text:
Dubai recorded 13,707 residential sales valued at AED 39.49bn in the last four weeks, representing a 24.1% increase in volume and a 23.1% rise in value compared to the previous four-week period. Mortgage registrations totaled 5,556, which are tracked separately from sales transactions. The off-plan segment accounted for 56.7% of all registered sales during this period.

The median residential price per square foot reached AED 1,727, marking a 3.4% increase from the prior four-week median of AED 1,671. In the rental market, 107,552 Ejari contracts were registered with a renewal share of 51.9%. The median annual residential rent stood at AED 68,000 for the same period.

Top performing areas by sales volume over the last 12 weeks include Dubai South with 2,736 transactions and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,521. Dubai South shows a 12-week price change of -3.9% and an estimated gross yield of 4.7%, while Jumeirah Village Circle is flat at 0.2% with a 6.3% yield. Dubai Creek Harbour recorded 849 sales with a 5.3% price increase and a 4.8% yield.

Watch-list highlights include Al Yufrah 1 with a 33.0% price increase and Dubai Industrial City up 10.4%. Conversely, Saih Shuaib 1 declined by 29.6% and Sama Al Jadaf by 14.1%. International City Phase 1 leads in estimated gross yield at 8.6% for flats, followed by Zaabeel First at 7.9%. An anomaly monitor flagged 956 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35% away from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
